newsitem.title: USA: USDA stands by 28 mln bag Brazil coffee estimate.
newsitem.headline: USDA stands by 28 mln bag Brazil coffee estimate.

text.p: The Agriculture Department said Wednesday it had confidence in its 28-million bag estimate of Brazil's 1997/98 coffee harvest, and that a lower estimate by a U.S. agricultural attache did not take into account all factors influencing the crop.
"We stand by our numbers and the integrity of our system," said Ed Cissel, director of production estimates and crop assessment for the USDA's Foreign Agricultural Service.
The Association of Coffee Producing Countries earlier Wednesday expressed concern about a four-million bag difference in a pair of recent crop estimates.
On June 13, the USDA issued its official Brazil crop estimate of 28 million bags. But a U.S. attache report, written May 12 and made public on Tuesday, pegged output at 24 million bags.
Meanwhile, the Brazilian government has forecast a harvest of 22 million bags, while trade sources have suggested that 23 to 25 million bags is the likely range of 1997/98 output.
Cissel said the attache reports were one of many pieces of information evaluated in preparing an official agency estimate.

"The attache reports come in from the field, and they are unofficial reports," Cissel said. "The information is evaluated here and the (USDA's) World Board evaluates the figures to make sure we come out with unbiased numbers."
"Our methodology is a convergence of evidence. We look at the attache reports, weather, statistical trends, trees planted and so forth," he said.
Cissel also defended the USDA estimates as objective and unbiased.
